addresses.loadFailed: Your addresses could not be loaded.
addresses.lastCannotBeRemoved: This is the only confirmed address on your account.

addresses.checkYourMail: Check that address for a link to confirm it.
addresses.addFailed: That address could not be added.
addresses.removeFailed: That address could not be removed.
addresses.primaryChanged: Your account mail goes there now.
addresses.primaryFailed: The primary address could not be changed.

addresses.addDialogDescription: We'll send a link to {{email}} to confirm it.
addresses.primaryDialogDescription: Password resets and sign-in codes will go to {{email}} first.

heldChange.secondFactorOff: Two-factor authentication will be turned off on {{date}}.
heldChange.lastPasskey: Your last passkey, {{subject}}, will be removed on {{date}}.

heldChange.applyNow: Make it now with a passkey

security.newKeyDescription: Copy this key now. You will not be able to view it again.
security.generateDescription: Create long-lived credentials for scripts or integrations.
security.readOnlyHelp: The key can read data but never create, change, or delete anything. Recommended for automation and integrations.
security.communityHelp: Limit the key to a single community. It won't be able to reach any other community's data.
security.signedInDescription: The browsers and devices currently signed in to your account. Signing one out ends that session only.
security.noSignedInHint: When you sign in from another browser or device, it will appear here.
security.signOutDialogDescription: This ends the session on <bold>{{deviceName}}</bold>. It will need to sign in again.
security.removeDeviceDialogDescription: <bold>{{deviceName}}</bold> is signed out and nothing more is sent to it. If it is ever signed in again, the messages only it held are deleted from it.
security.signOutOthersDialogDescription_one: This ends {{count}} other session. You'll stay signed in here.
security.signOutOthersDialogDescription_other: This ends all {{count}} other sessions. You'll stay signed in here.
security.apiKeysDescription: For scripts and integrations. A key's secret is shown once, when you create it.
security.deleteDialogDescription: Anything that uses {{name}} stops working straight away.

ai.httpWarning: Using an unencrypted HTTP endpoint. Configure TLS / HTTPS for production deployments.

communityAI.title: Community AI
communityAI.adminOnly: Only community admins can manage AI connections.
communityAI.connectionsDescription: Define the AI connections members of this community can use.
communityAI.disabledDescription: AI features are turned off for the platform.
communityAI.managedByPlatform: AI connections are managed at the platform level. Members set their own key in their profile settings.
communityAI.managedByServer: Whoever runs this server manages AI for this community.
communityAI.switchHelp: Off, nothing in this community is sent to an AI provider, whichever connection the server or the community sets up.

platformAI.title: Platform AI
platformAI.description: Choose how AI is configured across the platform. Like sign-in, AI is managed either by the platform or by each community — never both.
platformAI.platformOnly: Only platform owners can manage platform AI settings.
platformAI.mode_disabled_description: AI features are turned off for everyone.
platformAI.mode_platform_description: You define the AI connections every community uses.
platformAI.mode_community_description: Each community admin defines their own AI connections.
platformAI.connectionsDescription: Define the AI connections every community uses.

marketplaceRegistry.title: Marketplace registry
marketplaceRegistry.description: Plug-ins and content from the Initiative registry. Everything it brings is checked against the signing key built into this server before it is used.
marketplaceRegistry.toggleHelp: Off, this server stops asking the registry for updates. Listings and plug-ins it already brought stay.
marketplaceRegistry.enabledToast: This server follows the registry again.
marketplaceRegistry.disabledToast: This server no longer follows the registry.
marketplaceRegistry.notConfigured: This server has no registry signing key, so there is no registry to follow.
marketplaceRegistry.customRoot: This server uses a different registry signing key, set by MARKETPLACE_REGISTRY_ROOT.
marketplaceRegistry.fromBundle: The last update came from an uploaded bundle.
marketplaceRegistry.stale: The registry's signatures ran out on {{when}}. Its listings may be out of date until the next update.
marketplaceRegistry.skipped_one: {{count}} listing was skipped. The status below says why.
marketplaceRegistry.skipped_other: {{count}} listings were skipped. The status below says why.
marketplaceRegistry.bundleHelp: For a server without internet access: a .tar.gz of the registry's metadata and targets folders. It is checked against the same signing key.

interface.colorThemeDescription: Choose a color theme for the application.
interface.weekStartsOnDescription: Choose which day to show first on calendars and date pickers.

timeFormat.label: Time format
timeFormat.description: Show clock times as 1:30 PM or 13:30. Browser default follows your browser's language, which your operating system's clock setting does not change.

interface.recentTabsLimitDescription: How many recently-opened items to keep in the header tab bar (1–100).
interface.languageDescription: Choose your preferred language for the interface.

themeDescriptions.kobold: The classic Initiative theme with deep indigo tones.
themeDescriptions.strahd: Dark gothic theme with purple accents (Dracula/Alucard).
themeDescriptions.unicorn: Full-spectrum neon rainbow — loud and proud.
themeDescriptions.darkKnight: AMOLED black theme with dark red and yellow accents.
themeDescriptions.orc: Earthy green theme with vivid orc-skin green accents. ORC ORC ORC!
themeDescriptions.aboleth: Monokai-inspired dark lair with vivid bioluminescent accent colors.

taskCompletionVisualFeedback.label: Task completion feedback
taskCompletionVisualFeedback.description: A bit of fun when you finish a task you were assigned to.

taskCompletionAudioFeedback.label: Sound on task completion
taskCompletionAudioFeedback.description: Play a short pop sound when you finish any task.

taskCompletionHapticFeedback.label: Vibration on task completion
taskCompletionHapticFeedback.description: Briefly vibrate your device when you finish any task. Mobile / supported browsers only.

keepScreenAwake.label: Keep screen awake
keepScreenAwake.description: Prevent this device's screen from dimming or locking while the app is open.
keepScreenAwake.unsupported: Your browser does not support keeping the screen awake.

desktopKeepRunning.label: Keep running when the window closes
desktopKeepRunning.description: Stay in the tray so notifications still arrive. Quit from the tray icon.

desktopOpenAtLogin.label: Open when the computer starts
desktopOpenAtLogin.description: Start Initiative when you sign in to this computer.

desktopAutoUpdate.label: Update the app automatically
desktopAutoUpdate.description: When your server needs a newer desktop app, download it and install it on restart.

interface.addingDescription: How a task you are adding is filled in.

smartTaskTitles.label: Read details from the title
smartTaskTitles.description: Write “friday at 3pm”, “every week”, “!high”, “#tag” or “@name” in a new task's title to set its due date, repeat, priority, tags and assignees. What is read is highlighted; take it off to keep the words as they are.

interface.completionDescription: What the app does the moment a task is checked off. Try each one before you keep it.
interface.deviceDescription: Saved on this device only, not to your account.

notifications.title: Notification settings
notifications.pushDescription: Get alerts on this device as they happen.
notifications.pushBlockedDescription: To enable push notifications, open your device settings, find this app, and enable notifications.

reminderLeadTime.label: Remind me
reminderLeadTime.atStart: At the time of the event

notifications.channelsDescription: One row per kind of update, one switch per channel. Nothing is on that you have not left on.

categoryDescriptions.mentions: Somebody named you, replied to you or reacted to your comment.
categoryDescriptions.assignments: You were given a task or invited to something, or what you're on changed, was cancelled or is about to start.
categoryDescriptions.subscriptions: Changes, comments and reactions on what you follow, which includes what you made, and the reminders you set on tasks. The bell on anything stops its changes.
categoryDescriptions.news: A post went up, you were added to an initiative or a project, or your request to join was answered.
categoryDescriptions.approvals: Somebody is waiting on your decision. Always shows in the bell.
categoryDescriptions.moderation: A community's moderators took down or warned you about something you wrote. Always shows in the bell.
categoryDescriptions.cases: A case opened where you work cases, or its requester answered and nobody has taken it.
categoryDescriptions.direct_messages: Somebody messaged you, asked to connect, or accepted. Who and how many, never what a message says.
categoryDescriptions.jobs: An export or import you asked for has finished.
categoryDescriptions.account: Something was done to your account. Always shows in the bell.
categoryDescriptions.overdue: Every task assigned to you that is past its due date, in one message.
categoryDescriptions.coming_up: Tasks due and events starting before the next one, in one message.

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.description: Hold email, mobile and desktop overnight. The bell still collects, and one summary goes out when the window ends.

communities.title: Per community
communities.description: Switch a row off for one community, or mute it, without changing anything anywhere else.
communities.mutedHelp: This community says nothing at all — including if somebody names you directly.

timing.personalInstant: Send things addressed to me right away
timing.personalInstantHelp: Mentions, replies, tasks assigned to you, invitations and direct messages skip the queue.
timing.respectPresence: Don't interrupt me while I'm using Initiative
timing.respectPresenceHelp: If you're already here, the bell has told you. Email waits a few minutes and mobile stays quiet.

pause.title: Pause notifications
pause.description: Email, mobile and desktop stand down for the days you pick. The bell keeps collecting, and you get one summary of everything when you're back.
pause.help: Leave the start empty to begin now. Both days are included.
pause.note: Password resets and sign-in emails still arrive. Those aren't notifications.

timing.saveError: Unable to update when you hear about things

digests.title: Digests
digests.description: Summaries on a schedule. Everything in them is already in your bell.
digests.gatheredEmailHelp: Email from the rows above arrives right away, or gathered into one message.
digests.afterPause: When a pause or quiet hours end, you also get one summary of what came in.

dangerZone.disconnectDescription: Log out and disconnect from this server. You can connect to a different server afterward.
dangerZone.deactivateDescription: Temporarily disable your account. Your name, email, and content remain intact, but you'll be removed from every community you're a member of — rejoining requires a fresh invite. Whoever runs this server can reactivate your account later.
dangerZone.permanentDeleteDescriptionText: Your account disappears for everyone else straight away. Nothing is erased for a while yet — sign back in before then and the deletion is called off, with your communities and your work exactly as you left them. After that, projects are transferred to other people, and comments and files stay but show "[Deleted User]".
dangerZone.cannotBeUndone: Signing in is what stops it.
dangerZone.title: Close your account

deleteAccount.title: Delete Account
deleteAccount.chooseTypeDescription: Choose how you want to delete your account
deleteAccount.checkBlockersDescription: Checking if your account can be deleted
deleteAccount.checkBlockersDeactivateDescription: Checking if your account can be deactivated
deleteAccount.deactivateLabel: Deactivate my account (whoever runs this server can reactivate it later)
deleteAccount.deactivateRadioDescription: You will not be able to log in, and you'll be removed from every community you're in — rejoining requires a fresh invite. Whoever runs the server can reactivate your account on request. Your name, email, and content remain intact.
deleteAccount.softDeleteLabel: Delete my account (remove my personal information)
deleteAccount.softDeleteRadioDescription: Your name, email, and avatar will be removed and you will not be able to log in. Comments, tasks, and other content you authored will remain visible as "Deleted user". This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.soleSuperadminBlocker: You are the only superadmin of {{communityName}}. Make another member superadmin, or delete the community, first.
deleteAccount.resolveIssues: Please resolve these issues before deleting your account.
deleteAccount.resolveIssuesDeactivate: Please resolve these issues before deactivating your account.
deleteAccount.eligible: Your account is eligible for deletion.
deleteAccount.eligibleDeactivate: Your account is eligible for deactivation.
deleteAccount.deactivateConfirmDescription: Your account will be deactivated. You will not be able to log in until whoever runs this server reactivates it. You will be removed from every community you belong to, and rejoining will require a fresh invite. Your name, email, and content remain intact.
deleteAccount.softDeleteConfirmDescription: Your name, email, and avatar will be removed. You will not be able to log in. Comments, tasks, and other content you authored will remain visible as "Deleted user". This cannot be undone.

branding.platformOnly: Only the platform owner can manage branding settings.
branding.colorsDescription: Customize the accent colors for light and dark mode.
branding.lightModeHelp: Buttons, highlights, and focus states use this color while the app is in light mode.
branding.darkModeHelp: Accent and primary elements use this color while dark mode is active.

yonderPlayground.title: Yonder toast playground
yonderPlayground.description: Trigger each toast type to preview its Yonder variant and animation.

withDescription.label: with description
withDescription.detail: Your changes are now live across all devices.

cookieConsent.title: Cookie choices
cookieConsent.description: Ask arriving visitors what this deployment may keep in their browser.
cookieConsent.helpText: A chooser along the bottom of the page the first time somebody arrives: what is essential, and a switch for anything that isn't. Turn it on if this deployment has a public front door; leave it off for a server your group reaches by invitation, where it is only something in the way.
cookieConsent.scopeNote: Off is not a way to skip the question — it is for a deployment where nobody arrives who was not sent. With it off, everything optional stays off, because nothing may be switched on that was never agreed to.

email.platformOnly: Only the platform owner can manage email settings.
email.title: SMTP email
email.secureHelp: Enable for port 465. Keep disabled for ports 587 or 25 (uses STARTTLS when available).
email.rejectUnauthorizedHelp: Disable only if you fully trust the mail server and understand the risk.
email.passwordHelp: Leave blank to keep the existing password.

push.platformOnly: Only the platform owner can manage push notification settings.
push.loadError: Unable to load push notification settings.
push.title: Firebase Cloud Messaging
push.description: Optional. Without a service account key, push notifications go through BeyondersStudio's push relay and these fields can stay empty. With one, Android pushes go through your own Firebase project; iPhone pushes always use the relay.
push.enabledHelp: The mobile apps pick this up the next time they open. No restart needed.

application_id.label: App ID
application_id.help: Project settings → General → Your apps → App ID.

api_key.label: Web API key
api_key.help: Project settings → General → Web API key.

sender_id.label: Sender ID
sender_id.help: Project settings → Cloud Messaging → Sender ID.

push.serviceAccountSet: A key is saved. Paste a new one to replace it.
push.serviceAccountHelp: The whole JSON file from Project settings → Service accounts → Generate new private key. Leave blank to keep the saved key.
push.serviceAccountInvalid: Paste the whole key file: one JSON object, braces included.

captcha.title: Captcha
captcha.description: A check that the person signing up, or asking for an emailed sign-in code, is not a bot.
captcha.secretKeyHelp: Leave blank to keep the saved secret key.
captcha.incomplete: The captcha comes on once a provider, a site key and a secret key are all saved.

auth.platformOnly: Only the platform owner can manage authentication settings.

methods.title: Ways in
methods.description: How people may sign in to this deployment. At least one way of starting a session stays on.

password.label: Password
password.help: An email address and a password held here.

methods.lastRemaining: The last way in cannot be withdrawn.
methods.wouldStrand_one: {{count}} account signs in only this way.
methods.wouldStrand_other: {{count}} accounts sign in only this way.
methods.confirmBody_one: {{count}} account signs in only this way and will not be able to sign in until it has another. Nobody is signed out.
methods.confirmBody_other: {{count}} accounts sign in only this way and will not be able to sign in until they have another. Nobody is signed out.
methods.saveError: Could not change the ways in.
methods.communitiesRequire_one: {{count}} community requires a sign-in through a provider of its own.
methods.communitiesRequire_other: {{count}} communities require a sign-in through a provider of their own.

totp.label: Enable two-factor authentication
totp.help: Let people protect their account with a code from an authenticator app. Each person turns it on for themselves; this is whether the server offers it at all.

passkey.label: Passkey
passkey.help: A key held by a device or a password manager, answering a prompt instead of a password. People add them for themselves.

email_otp.label: Email OTP
email_otp.help: A one-time code sent to an address the account holds, typed back into the sign-in page. Every account with an address can use it, so it stays off until you turn it on.

sessionLifetime.title: How long people stay signed in
sessionLifetime.description: The longest anybody may go before signing in again, however much they use the app. Separate from being signed out for not using it.
sessionLifetime.label: Hours
sessionLifetime.hint: Leave blank for no limit. A figure shorter than the inactivity window becomes the only thing ending a session. Web sessions already open keep their original terms; phones are brought under a shortened limit straight away.
sessionLifetime.error: We couldn't save the session limit.
sessionLifetime.idleHint: How long a session may sit untouched before it ends. Leave blank to keep the window set when the server was deployed. Using the app counts as touching it, so this only runs down once somebody has stopped. A community held to the compliance standard shortens it further for its own members.

breachedPasswordCheck.title: Breached passwords
breachedPasswordCheck.description: Turn away a new password that has already turned up in a data breach.
breachedPasswordCheck.label: Check new passwords against known breaches
breachedPasswordCheck.onHelp: Only the first five characters of the password's hash leave this server. The password itself never does.
breachedPasswordCheck.offHelp: New passwords are not checked. Turn this off only where this server cannot reach the internet.
breachedPasswordCheck.enabledToast: New passwords are checked against known breaches.
breachedPasswordCheck.disabledToast: New passwords are no longer checked against known breaches.
breachedPasswordCheck.error: We couldn't change the breached password check.

secondFactorRequirement.title: Two-factor authentication
secondFactorRequirement.description: Whether people here have to hold a second factor — an authenticator app or a passkey — as well as a way to sign in.

nobody.label: Nobody has to
nobody.help: Anybody can set one up, and nobody is asked to. Where this is what you want, communities can still ask for one of their own.

platform_roles.label: People with a platform role
platform_roles.help: Support, moderators, operators and owners — everybody whose reach is the whole server rather than the communities they belong to.

everyone.label: Everybody
everyone.help: Every account on this server. Communities stop being offered the question, because it is already answered for their members.

secondFactorRequirement.wouldAsk_one: {{count}} person doesn't have one yet. They'll be asked to set one up the next time they open the app.
secondFactorRequirement.wouldAsk_other: {{count}} people don't have one yet. They'll be asked to set one up the next time they open the app.
secondFactorRequirement.derivedCredentials: Personal API keys and the app on a phone can't present a code, so they stop working for anybody this covers until that person sets a factor up — and work again as soon as they do.
secondFactorRequirement.unmet: Set up a second factor of your own first, then save.
secondFactorRequirement.saved: Saved. People this covers are asked at their next request.
secondFactorRequirement.noMethod: Permit the authenticator app or passkeys first — with neither offered there is nothing to ask people for.

providers.title: Providers whose sign-in counts
providers.help: A sign-in through one of these answers the requirement above, because the provider reports running a second factor of its own. The same answer as on the provider's own page.

factorMethods.title: Two-factor authentication
factorMethods.description: What this server offers as a second factor. Whether anybody has to hold one is the next setting.
factorMethods.followsWaysIn: A passkey proves the device and the person in one go, so it answers this as well as opening a session. Whether passkeys are offered is decided under Ways in.

platformUsers.resetDescription: Send a password reset to {{handle}}? They'll get a link at the address they signed up with.
platformUsers.resendVerificationError: Unable to send the verification email
platformUsers.permissionRequired: You don't have permission to view platform users.

roleDescriptions.member: Standard access to their own communities. No platform-wide privileges.
roleDescriptions.support: Read-only platform visibility (users, communities) and can request time-bound access to a community.
roleDescriptions.moderator: Everything Support can do, plus user management (suspend/reactivate) and content moderation.
roleDescriptions.operator: Manages users, communities, and roles platform-wide, with cross-community data access and approves access requests.
roleDescriptions.owner: Full control, including app-wide configuration (auth, branding, email, AI). The only role that can manage configuration.

platformUsers.changeRoleDescription: This will change {{email}}'s platform role to {{role}}.
platformUsers.suspendBody: They keep everything — memberships, sharing, and everything they have written — and reach nothing until this is lifted. They can still sign in, and see only that they are suspended, your reason, and whom to contact.
platformUsers.actionError: That could not be done. Try again.
platformUsers.ageBlockCleared: They can answer the age question again.
platformUsers.signInLockLifted: They can sign in with a password again.
platformUsers.clearSecondFactorDescription: Take the authenticator off {{handle}}'s account? This is for when they've lost their phone and their recovery codes. They're signed out everywhere and emailed about it, then sign in the way they usually do and can set it up again.
platformUsers.secondFactorCleared: Two-factor authentication cleared. They can sign in the way they usually do.

sheet.description: What an operator keeps for this account. Each change saves on its own.
sheet.usernameHelp: The handle they are addressed by. The number after it stays as it is.
sheet.avatarHelp: Take the picture down. It cannot be replaced from here.
sheet.avatarConfirmBody: The picture on {{handle}} comes down and they are told. They can upload another.
sheet.apiKeysHelp_one: {{count}} key still works. Revoking switches it off now; they can make a new one.
sheet.apiKeysHelp_other: {{count}} keys still work. Revoking switches them off now; they can make new ones.
sheet.apiKeysConfirmBody_one: {{handle}}'s key stops working at once. It stays on their list marked disabled, and they can make a new one.
sheet.apiKeysConfirmBody_other: All {{count}} of {{handle}}'s keys stop working at once. They stay on their list marked disabled, and they can make new ones.
sheet.suspendHelp: A suspended account can sign in and read why, and reaches nothing else.
sheet.roleHelp: What this account may do across the whole deployment. You cannot grant above your own role.
sheet.signOutHelp: End every session on every device. They sign in again; anyone else who had the account does not.
sheet.signOutConfirmBody: Every session {{handle}} has ends now, on every device, and its open connections close. They can sign in again.

displayNames.label: Names in communities
displayNames.help: The names they go by in their communities, all of them. They can set them again.
displayNames.confirmBody: The names {{handle}} goes by in every community are cleared, and their handle shows instead. They can set them again.

customStatus.label: Status line
customStatus.help: The status line shown beside their name. They can set another.
customStatus.confirmBody: The status line on {{handle}} is cleared. They can set another.

decorations.label: Decorations
decorations.help: Their profile banner, frame and trophies. They can set them again.
decorations.confirmBody: The banner, frame and trophies on {{handle}} are taken off. They can set them again.

cases.title: Cases
cases.count_one: {{count}} open case they filed or that is about them.
cases.count_other: {{count}} open cases they filed or that are about them.
cases.help: Opening a case needs access to the project it is kept in.

sheet.forCaseHelp: Optional. What you do here is noted on the case you choose.
sheet.reactivateHelp: Bring the account back. It returns with no communities; they rejoin the ones they want.
sheet.restoreHelp: Call off the deletion. Everything is where it was, communities included. Signing in does the same.
sheet.ageBlockHelp: Let them answer it again, for a mistyped year. Nothing else changes.
sheet.resetHelp: Email them a link to choose a new one.
sheet.resendHelp: Not confirmed yet. Send the confirmation letter again.
sheet.signInLockHelp: Turned off after too many wrong answers. Turn it back on.
sheet.secondFactorHelp: Take off an authenticator they've lost. They're signed out everywhere and set one up again.
sheet.deleteHelp: Deactivate it, schedule its deletion, or delete it for good. You choose which next.

platformUsers.restoreError: Could not restore the account. Please try again.

operatorDeleteUser.subtitle: Delete {{email}}
operatorDeleteUser.deactivateDescription: User cannot log in. PII preserved. Reversible from the users page.
operatorDeleteUser.softDeleteDescription: The account disappears for everyone else and keeps everything it holds. It is erased when the deployment's window ends, unless its holder signs back in or you restore it.
operatorDeleteUser.hardDeleteDescription: All user data is removed from the database. Comments, tasks, and other content authored by this user are deleted via cascade. Cannot be reversed.
operatorDeleteUser.blockersDescription: The following issues must be resolved before this user can be deleted:
operatorDeleteUser.communityBlockerDescription: The account holder can make another member superadmin, or you can break glass into the community and, from its settings, appoint one or delete the community.
operatorDeleteUser.confirmDeactivate: Deactivate {{email}} — they cannot log in but their data is preserved.
operatorDeleteUser.confirmSoftDelete: Anonymize {{email}} — PII is removed. Comments and tasks they authored remain visible as "Deleted user". This cannot be reversed.
operatorDeleteUser.confirmHardDelete: Permanently delete {{email}} — the row and all cascading data are removed. This cannot be reversed.
operatorDeleteUser.preferWindowLabel: Delete with the recovery window instead
operatorDeleteUser.preferWindowHelp: The account keeps everything and disappears for everyone else. It is erased at the end of the window unless somebody brings it back.

accessGrants.description: Request and approve time-bound access to a community you're not a member of.
accessGrants.requestDescription: Ask for temporary, scoped access to a community. Approvers grant it and it auto-expires.

breakGlass.title: Break glass
breakGlass.description: Self-issue emergency access to a community — approved instantly, scoped to that community, and auto-expiring. Read & write acts as a full community admin. Every break-glass grant is recorded.
breakGlass.reasonPlaceholder: Why you need emergency access (e.g. incident #123)
breakGlass.codeHelp: Two-factor authentication is turned on for this server, so breaking glass asks you to prove it is you. An authenticator code, a recovery code or one of your passkeys will do.
breakGlass.codeNotEnrolled: This account has no authenticator and no passkey. Set one up under Security, then break glass.

accessGrants.queueDescription: Grant, deny, or revoke time-bound access requests.
accessGrants.nothingAsked: Choose content access, settings access, or both.
accessGrants.purposeContentHelp: Read, or edit, what is inside the community.
accessGrants.purposeSettingsHelp: Its configuration only — billing, sign-in, moderation.
accessGrants.caseRequiredHint: Choose the case this access is for.
accessGrants.caseRequiredNoneOpen: Access is asked for on a case here, and there is no open case you can name. Open one first.
accessGrants.caseOptionalHint: Optional. Without one, record what you did on the case by hand afterwards.
accessGrants.caseOtherCommunity: This case is about community #{{community}}, not the one chosen.

notice.label: Tell the community
notice.help: Its superadmins are emailed the level and the kind of case, never the reason.
notice.always: Access for a support case is always emailed to the community's superadmins when it starts.

pluginServices.platformOnly: Only platform owners can manage plug-in services.
pluginServices.title: Plug-in services
pluginServices.description: The plug-ins this deployment runs. A plug-in's listing says what it is and may do; here you give where it answers and the keys it signs with.
pluginServices.empty: No plug-in services yet. A plug-in appears here when its listing arrives, or once you add it.
pluginServices.declarativeSummary: Initiative makes this plug-in's calls itself. It needs no address or keys, only its vendor values.
pluginServices.needsAddress: Runs as a container. Edit it and give the address where you run it to make it live.
pluginServices.disabledHelp: This plug-in is stopped for every community that installed it. Nothing has been deleted.
pluginServices.publisherDisabledHelp: Every plug-in from {{name}} is stopped because its publisher is switched off. Nothing has been deleted.
pluginServices.noKeysHelp: Not live until it has signing keys. Edit it to paste a key set or give its address.
pluginServices.mandatoryHelp: Installed into every community automatically. Community admins cannot remove it or turn it off.
pluginServices.operationsOnlyHelp: Only the operations community can find and install it. Copies installed in any other community stop working. Nothing is deleted.
pluginServices.operationsMandatoryHelp: Turned on with Install in every community, it's added to the operations community only, and its admins cannot remove it or turn it off.
pluginServices.sharedRoutesHelp: Lets one installation at the vendor, such as a GitHub organization, connect to several communities on this server. It can be turned off once each installation is connected to one community.
pluginServices.keysHelp: The public keys this plug-in signs its access-token assertions with. The plug-in is live only once it has a pasted key set or a key set address. It can have both.
pluginServices.jwksHelp: Paste the key set the plug-in publishes, or press Connect on a saved plug-in to read it from the plug-in. Two entries mean a rotation is in flight. Clearing the box removes it.
pluginServices.jwksUriHelp: Where the plug-in publishes its key set, so a key rotation needs no edit here. It must be https on the base URL's own origin; the server refuses any other address. Clearing the field removes it.
pluginServices.connectHelp: Read the key set the plug-in serves at its saved base URL, and pin it in place of any key set address once you confirm its fingerprints.
pluginServices.connectSaveFirst: Save the new base URL, then connect.
pluginServices.connectKeysHelp: Check each fingerprint against the one the plug-in's container logs when it starts (app key fingerprint: …). Pin them only if they match.
pluginServices.connected: Keys pinned. A new key set from the plug-in is used only after you connect again.
pluginServices.connectError: Could not read the plug-in's keys.
pluginServices.vendorHelp: What this plug-in's vendor issued for this server. Initiative uses it to connect communities and members to the vendor. A secret is never shown again once saved; type a new one to replace it.
pluginServices.vendorMissingHelp: Not live until its vendor client is set. Edit it to fill in the values the plug-in asks for.
pluginServices.redirectTitle: Addresses to register with the vendor
pluginServices.redirectHelp: Add these to the vendor's settings for this client. It sends people back to the callback and setup addresses, and its webhooks to the webhook address.
pluginServices.composeHelp: Add this service to the docker-compose.yml that runs Initiative, then run docker compose up -d. The base URL below is where it answers on the Compose network.
pluginServices.vendorSetupHelp: GitHub opens with this plug-in's permissions, events and Initiative's addresses filled in. Confirm it there, and GitHub sends the new app's values back here, so you type and copy none of them.
pluginServices.vendorSetupOrganizationHelp: The organization that owns the new app. Leave blank to create it under your own GitHub account.
pluginServices.vendorSetupError: Could not start the setup at GitHub.
pluginServices.vendorSetupDone: GitHub App created. Its values are saved.
pluginServices.vendorSetupFailed: Could not save the GitHub App's values.
pluginServices.createDescription: Give a plug-in its address and keys before its listing arrives. What it is and may do comes from its listing. It goes live once it has signing keys.
pluginServices.editDescription: Changes apply to every community that installed this plug-in.
pluginServices.publicIdHelp: Written as publisher.plugin-name, in lowercase. The part before the dot is the plug-in's publisher.
pluginServices.publicIdHelpEdit: The identifier cannot be changed once the registration exists.
pluginServices.baseUrlHelp: Where Initiative's server calls the plug-in. This may be a private address inside your own network.
pluginServices.pageOriginHelp: Where a member's browser loads this plug-in's pages and connection pages. Leave blank when the plug-in answers at the base URL for both.
pluginServices.allowedOriginsHelp: One per line. Leave blank to allow only the browser address's own origin.
pluginServices.allowedOriginsHelpEdit: One per line. Leave blank to keep the current origins.
pluginServices.saveError: Could not save the plug-in service.
pluginServices.deleteError: Could not delete the plug-in service.
pluginServices.toggleError: Could not change the plug-in service.
pluginServices.disableDescription: Every community that installed this plug-in stops reaching it immediately — data, configuration, events, and pages all refuse. Nothing is deleted, and you can turn it back on at any time.
pluginServices.deleteDescription: The registration is removed for good. Every community that installed this plug-in stops reaching it, and adding it back means registering it again.
pluginServices.deleteConfirmLabel: Type the plug-in identifier to confirm

communities.title: Community limits
communities.description: Set per-community caps on storage and on the number of users. Lowering a limit below current usage blocks new uploads or members, but never removes existing files or members.
communities.platformOnly: You need a platform staff role to see communities.
communities.loadError: Could not load communities. Please try again.
communities.helpText: Storage limits are in GB; user limits are a member count. Both save automatically — leave a field blank for unlimited.
communities.helpTextBilling: Billing sets each community's limits, features and status. You can suspend a community here, and lifting the suspension returns it to the status billing last set.
communities.saveError: Could not update the storage limit. Please try again.
communities.statusSaveError: Could not update the community status. Please try again.

suspendConfirm.title: Suspend {{name}}?
suspendConfirm.description: Everyone in it loses all access, its administrators included, until you lift it. Members stop seeing it; administrators see it closed. Nothing is deleted, and operators keep access through a break-glass grant.

holdConfirm.title: Put {{name}} on hold?
holdConfirm.description: Everyone in it loses all access, its administrators included, and it leaves every list. Nothing is deleted. Its superadmins are told once, by email and in the app, whom to contact.

billing.openError: Could not open the billing portal.

factor.title: Confirm it's you
factor.description: Opening billing for {{name}} issues you a billing grant. Enter a code from your authenticator app or a recovery code.

sheet.description: Settings only you can change. This community's own admins see them and cannot edit them.
sheet.usersHelp: How many people may belong. Leave blank for no limit.
sheet.guestsHelp: How many guests they may have at once. 0 takes no new guests, and those already in stay until their time ends. Leave blank for no limit.
sheet.storageHelp: How much they may store, in gigabytes. Leave blank for no limit.
sheet.bannerHelp: Let them upload a banner image. Without it they pick a banner colour instead, and any banner already uploaded keeps showing.
sheet.supportHelp: Let their members send a help request. Off, the Ask for help control opens the FAQ instead.
sheet.supportNeedsIntake: Nowhere to send a help request yet. Bind the support stream to a project under Platform settings › Intake, and this can be switched on.
sheet.aiConnectionsHelp: Lets the community set up AI providers of its own. Off, the ones it has are kept and not used.
sheet.pluginsHelp: Lets the community install and configure plug-ins. Off, the ones it has keep running as they are.
sheet.customRolesHelp: Its admins can define roles that give people part of running the community. Closed, the roles it has keep applying.

restrictions.label: Its own security standard
restrictions.help: Its admins can refuse personal API keys and hold members to a twelve-hour session. For communities answering to an auditor; most never need it.

providers.label: Its own sign-in
providers.help: Its admins say which of this deployment's sign-in providers count as theirs, where the people arriving on them land — including as an admin of their community — and whether members must arrive that way.

sheet.pluginSummariesUnavailable: Plug-in usage could not be loaded.

narrowings.title: Who it counts as its own
narrowings.help: This community says which arrivals on a provider are its people. It names the values itself, so agreeing is what lets them join on arrival — until then the connection works only for the people already in it.
narrowings.joinsOnArrival: Asks that matching arrivals join on sight.
narrowings.admitsOnly: Admits matching arrivals; does not join anybody.

sheet.setInBilling: Billing sets this community's limits and features.

restore.purgesOn: Deleted. Everything in it is destroyed on {{date}}.
restore.purgesSoon: Deleted. Everything in it is destroyed when the retention window ends.
restore.retained: Until then nothing has been removed — restoring brings the community back exactly as it was, apart from its plug-in connections.
restore.title: Restore {{name}}
restore.seatDescription: Nobody is left who can run this community. Choose who takes it over.
restore.seatHelp: They become its superadmin: the seat that appoints others, reaches billing and sets sign-in.
restore.statusDescription: Choose what the community comes back as.
restore.pluginsNote: Its plug-in connections were ended when it was deleted and do not come back. Its admins can reconnect them.
restore.error: Could not restore the community. Please try again.

suspension.liftDescription: It returns to the status it had before: {{status}}. Everyone in it has the access they had then.
suspension.liftToDeleted: It goes back to being deleted, and the countdown to its destruction starts again from the beginning, so its owners have the whole window to restore it.
suspension.suspendDeleted: This community is deleted. Suspending it stops the countdown to its destruction until the suspension is lifted. Nobody in it can reach it either way.

providerPlacement.description: Place the people a sign-in provider signs in — by the group or directory it reports — in a community, and in an initiative there if you name one.
providerPlacement.loadError: Could not load placement rules. Please try again.
providerPlacement.platformOnly: Sign-in placement is managed by platform operators and owners.

everywhere.label: Apply placement rules to every community
everywhere.help: On, a rule places people in the community it names whether or not that community accepted. Every change is recorded.
everywhere.confirmTitle: Apply placement rules to every community?
everywhere.confirmDescription: Every rule then places people in the community it names, including communities that have not accepted its provider's rules. The change is recorded in the audit log.
everywhere.enabled: Placement rules now apply to every community
everywhere.disabled: Placement rules now apply where a community accepted them
everywhere.error: Could not change where placement rules apply

providerPlacement.noProviders: No sign-in providers yet. Once one is added on the Authentication page, its placement rules are written here.
providerPlacement.noGroups: This provider reports no groups yet: a rule naming a group matches nobody until an owner sets the provider's groups claim on the Authentication page. Rules naming only a directory work already.
providerPlacement.empty: No rules for this provider yet.
providerPlacement.addDescription: Say who this rule matches on {{provider}}, and where they land.
providerPlacement.editDescription: Places people from {{provider}} in {{community}}. A rule keeps its provider and community; for another, add a new rule.
providerPlacement.notApplyingHint: The community hasn't accepted this provider's rules, and they don't apply everywhere.
providerPlacement.groupHelp: Exactly as the provider spells it. Leave it empty to place everybody from the directory below.
providerPlacement.directoryHelp: For a provider that signs people in from several directories: the claim that names the directory, and this directory's value.
providerPlacement.needsMatch: Name a group, a directory, or both.
providerPlacement.communityHelp: A community marked Not accepted takes this provider's rules once it accepts them on its Security page.
providerPlacement.targetsUnavailable: Initiatives are listed once this community takes this provider's rules.
providerPlacement.removeDescription: People it matches stop being placed in {{community}} by it, and what it gave them is released the next time they sign in through this provider.

requests.title: Waiting for an answer
requests.help: These communities named a domain or tenant as their own on a connection. Agreeing lets the people it matches join them on arrival, where they asked for that.

storage.platformOnly: Only platform owners can configure storage.
storage.title: Object storage
storage.description: Choose where uploaded files and attachments are stored. Defaults to the local filesystem; switch to an S3-compatible store for scalable or shared deployments.
storage.backendHelp: Local stores files on the server disk. S3 works with any S3-compatible store, such as a self-hosted Garage or MinIO instance, or Cloudflare R2.
storage.cutoverTitle: Switching to S3 doesn't move existing files
storage.cutoverHelp: Save these settings, run Test connection, then use Backfill below to copy existing local files into the bucket. Switch the backend to S3 only once the backfill completes — optionally keep "Serve missing objects from local" on during a verification window.
storage.endpointHelp: The address of your store's S3 API.
storage.accessKeyPlaceholder: Leave blank to use the ambient credential chain
storage.secretKeyHelp: Leave blank to keep the stored key. Stored encrypted; never displayed.
storage.pathStyleHelp: Required for Garage and most self-hosted stores.
storage.localFallbackHelp: During cutover, read blobs not yet copied to S3 from the local disk.
storage.backfillHelp: Copies every existing local upload into the configured bucket. Idempotent and safe to re-run; run it before switching the backend to S3.

communityAuth.setByDeployment: Whoever runs this server sets this for your community.

shareUrl.title: Member sign-in link
shareUrl.description: Share this link with members — it offers this community's sign-in providers and brings them straight into the community.

policy.title: Sign-in requirement
policy.description: Control which sign-in a session must have used before it can access this community.
policy.openHelp: Any signed-in member can access this community.
policy.requiredHelp: Members can only access this community after signing in with the selected provider.
policy.noProviders: Connect a provider under Who gets in first.
policy.error: Could not save the sign-in requirement
policy.selfUnsatisfied: Your current session hasn't signed in with {{providerName}} yet. Sign in with it once to confirm it works before requiring it.
policy.unmetFactor: Enter a code from your authenticator app first, then save.
policy.unmetPasskey: Present your passkey first, then save.
policy.anyProviderHelp: Members can come in through any provider this community has set up. Signing in somewhere else on this deployment does not count.
policy.requireFactorHelp: Members must have presented a code from their authenticator app in this session. They can add one without signing out.
policy.requirePasskeyHelp: Members must have signed in with a passkey, or presented one, in this session. They can add one without signing out.
policy.factorRequiredByPlatform: Your server already asks everybody here for a second factor, so there's nothing to add.

sessionLimit.title: Session length
sessionLimit.allowLabel: Sign in again every twelve hours
sessionLimit.error: Could not save the session limit
sessionLimit.help: For communities that have been asked to cap how long people stay signed in. It applies to your members everywhere, not only here.

connections.title: Which sign-ins are yours
connections.description: People sign in to this deployment. Say which of its sign-in providers count as your community's, and who on them counts as yours.
connections.disconnectDescription: It stops counting as yours: the button comes off your sign-in page and nobody new arrives through it. Nobody is signed out and no account changes. If you require a sign-in through it, lift that first.
connections.empty: No providers connected yet — your members sign in the usual way.
connections.noneOffered: Whoever runs this deployment has not offered any providers to connect to yet.
connections.dialogDescription: Pick the provider your members use, then say which accounts on it are yours.
connections.claimHelp: Communities here are separate, so say which accounts on this provider are yours — a Google Workspace domain, an Entra tenant, a group. Only those people count as your community's.
connections.autoJoinHelp: Anyone who counts as yours becomes a member the first time they sign in. Leave it off to invite people yourself.
connections.joinsOnceAgreed: Will join matching arrivals on sight once whoever runs this server agrees these values are yours. Until then it admits them, and joining is by invitation.
connections.acceptsPlacementLabel: Let the deployment place people from this provider
connections.acceptsPlacementHelp: The deployment's placement rules for this provider can add people here, beside your own rules.

rules.title: Where your people land
rules.description: Your provider reports which groups somebody is in. Say what those groups mean here — who joins as a member, who joins as an admin, and which initiative they start in.
rules.empty: No rules yet — people arriving through your providers join with nothing in particular.
rules.connectFirst: Connect a provider first, then say what its groups mean.
rules.noGroupsHint: Whoever runs this deployment has not told this provider where its groups live, so this rule will not match anybody until they do.
rules.landsInInitiative: Arriving through {{provider}} — joins as {{role}}, and {{initiative}} as {{initiativeRole}}
rules.dialogDescription: Name a group your provider reports, and say where the people in it belong.
rules.groupHint: Exactly as your provider spells it.
rules.removeDescription: People carrying {{group}} stop being placed here, and anyone this rule put here loses that standing the next time they sign in through that provider.

deployment.title: Set by the deployment
deployment.description: Placement rules whoever runs this deployment wrote for its providers, naming this community. They place people here beside your own rules once you let a provider's rules in on its connection.
deployment.everywhere: The deployment applies its placement rules to every community.

emptyState.title: Nothing connected yet
emptyState.body: Say which of this deployment's sign-in providers count as yours, and where the people arriving on them land.

provider.title: Which way in
provider.prompt: Pick the provider your members already sign in with.

narrowing.title: Whose people
narrowing.prompt: Say which accounts on it count as yours.

landing.title: Where they land
landing.prompt: What happens when one of them arrives.

insist.title: Do we insist
insist.prompt: Whether this becomes the only way in.

wizard.ruleHelp: Optional. Name a group your provider reports and where its people land. You can add more later.
wizard.requireLabel: Require members to arrive through this provider
wizard.requireHelp: Members sign in through it and nothing else. You can change this later.

secondFactor.title: Second factor
secondFactor.description: Whether reaching this community asks for one.
secondFactor.help: Members must have presented a second factor in this session. Which kinds count is the deployment's answer, not this community's — they can add one without signing out.
secondFactor.askedByPlatform: Your server already asks everybody here for a second factor, so there's nothing to add.
secondFactor.error: Could not save the second-factor requirement.

guestPolicy.title: Guests' sign-in requirement
guestPolicy.description: Control which sign-in a guest's session must have used before it can reach this community. You don't have to meet it yourself.
guestPolicy.openHelp: Any signed-in guest can reach what they were given.
guestPolicy.requiredHelp: Guests can only reach this community after signing in with the selected provider.
guestPolicy.anyProviderHelp: Guests can come in through any provider this community has set up. Signing in somewhere else on this deployment does not count.
guestPolicy.requirePasskeyHelp: Guests must have signed in with a passkey, or presented one, in this session. They can add one without signing out.
guestPolicy.error: Could not save the guests' sign-in requirement

guestStay.title: Guest stays
guestStay.description: Guest invites and extensions never run longer than this. Guests already here keep their end date.
guestStay.label: Longest a guest may stay (days)
guestStay.hint_one: Leave blank to use the server's limit of {{count}} day, which is also the most you can set.
guestStay.hint_other: Leave blank to use the server's limit of {{count}} days, which is also the most you can set.
guestStay.error: Could not save the longest guest stay

authProviders.title: Identity providers
authProviders.description: The single sign-on providers people sign in with. Each one gets its own button on the sign-in page.
authProviders.dialogDescription: OpenID Connect provider details. The callback URL for your IdP is /api/v1/auth/{slug}/callback on this server.
authProviders.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes. Fixed after creation — it forms the sign-in URLs.
authProviders.slugInvalid: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes; no leading or trailing dash.
authProviders.secretPlaceholder: Leave blank for a public (PKCE-only) client
authProviders.secretKeepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the current secret
authProviders.allowJitHelp: When off, only existing accounts can sign in with this provider.
authProviders.assertsSecondFactorLabel: Its word counts for a second factor
authProviders.assertsSecondFactorHelp: When this provider says it ran a second factor, a sign-in through it answers a requirement for one. Leave it off unless you know it reports that honestly — people signing in through it are then asked for a factor of their own.
authProviders.deleteDescription: Accounts keep their other sign-in methods, but links to this provider are removed permanently.
authProviders.claimPathHelp: Where this provider puts a person's groups in the token. Keycloak nests them at realm_access.roles; most others use groups or roles. Each community's rules read it.
authProviders.scopesFromProvider: Filled in from what this provider says it offers.

wizard.title: Connect a sign-in provider
wizard.choosePrompt: Who are people signing in with?
wizard.credentialsPrompt: Register Initiative with {{name}}, then paste what it gives you.
wizard.optionsPrompt: How it behaves once somebody signs in.
wizard.callbackHelp: Your provider will refuse the sign-in until this exact address is registered with it.

presetHints.keycloak: From your realm's OpenID Connect client, with client authentication on.
presetHints.authentik: The application slug, not the provider name — the issuer follows the application.
presetHints.authelia: Paste the plaintext client secret, not the hash you put in the YAML.
presetHints.pocketId: Passkey-only, so your sign-ins inherit passkeys with nothing further to do.
presetHints.salesforce: Sandboxes and My Domain orgs each sign in at their own address, so use the one your people actually use rather than the generic login host.
presetHints.dex: The address ends with whatever your Dex config sets as its issuer — /dex by convention. It has to match that exactly.
presetHints.custom: Any provider that speaks OpenID Connect. Paste its issuer address — a .well-known URL works too.

aiConnections.title: Connections
aiConnections.subtitle: Each connection is a destination — a provider, model, and optional shared key.
aiConnections.empty: No connections yet. Add one to enable AI features.
aiConnections.deleteDescription: "{{label}}" will be removed. Members using it will lose access.
aiConnections.platformDialogDescription: Every community can use this connection.
aiConnections.communityDialogDescription: Members of this community can use this connection.
aiConnections.apiKeyHelpExisting: Leave blank to keep the existing key. Changing the provider or address clears it.
aiConnections.apiKeyHelpNew: The shared key all members use for this connection.
aiConnections.modelSearchPlaceholder: Search or type a model name…
aiConnections.modelsEmpty: No models to suggest — type the name
aiConnections.modelHintNew: Save to choose from the provider's models, or type a model's name.
aiConnections.modelHintPick: Pick a model to finish setting up this connection.
aiConnections.customHint: Any server that speaks the OpenAI API: vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI, or a gateway such as LiteLLM. Give the address up to /v1.
aiConnections.enabledDescription: Allow members to use this connection.
aiConnections.defaultDescription: Members use this connection unless they pick another.
aiConnections.communitiesHelpNone: It serves every community no other connection is given to.
aiConnections.communitiesHelpGiven: It serves only these communities. A community given here leaves any other connection it was given to.

community.title: Community directory
community.description: Let communities list themselves where anyone signed in can find them and join without an invite.
community.helpText: Turns on the public community directory: a browsable list of the communities that have chosen to be found. People search it and ask to join, and “Join a community” appears beside their own. Each community lists itself from its own settings.
community.reversibleNote: Turning it off closes the directory. Communities that listed themselves stay listed, and appear again when you turn it back on.
community.saveError: Could not change the community directory. Please try again.
community.platformOnly: You need the platform owner role to run a community directory.
community.ageGateHelpText: While this is on, sign-up asks for a date of birth and turns away anyone under the minimum age for an account where they are. Joining a listed community from the directory, opening direct messages and using a plug-in with a minimum age also need that answer. Invited communities never ask. Turn it off only where you already know every account belongs to an adult.
community.ageGateOffBody: Turning this off asserts that every account on this deployment belongs to someone 18 or older. Nobody will be asked their age again, and plug-ins with a minimum age open for everyone.
community.defaultDmHelpText: The policy an account starts on. Read once, when the account is made — changing it opens no account that already exists and closes none either. “Private” is the shipped default; on it, people become reachable one at a time as they choose to be.
community.directMessagesHelpText: My Messages, and the connections and requests behind it. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, so nobody running this deployment can read them — turn this off where private messaging does not belong rather than to oversee it.
community.directMessagesReversibleNote: Turning this off hides My Messages and refuses new ones; it deletes nothing. Conversations, connections and settings are all still there if you turn it back on.
community.directMessagesOffBody: My Messages will disappear for everyone here, and messages already on their way will not be delivered. Nothing is deleted, so turning it back on restores the conversations and connections people already had.

holdDeletion.title: Deleting communities on hold
holdDeletion.description: A community on hold is closed to everyone in it. If the hold is still in place when this window ends, the community is deleted, and the window above then decides how long it is kept. The people who run it are told the date when it goes on hold.
holdDeletion.label: Delete after (days on hold)
holdDeletion.hint: Counted from the moment each community was put on hold, so changing this moves the date for ones already on hold.
holdDeletion.neverHint: Nothing is deleted on a timer. A community stays on hold until somebody lifts the hold or deletes it.
holdDeletion.saved_one: Communities on hold are deleted after {{count}} day.
holdDeletion.saved_other: Communities on hold are deleted after {{count}} days.
holdDeletion.savedNever: Communities on hold are never deleted automatically.
holdDeletion.save: Save how long communities stay on hold

retention.title: Keeping deleted communities
retention.description: A deleted community disappears for everyone in it straight away, but nothing is destroyed until this window ends. Until then an operator can restore it.
retention.label: Keep communities for (days)
retention.hint: Counted from the moment each community was deleted, so changing this moves the date for ones already deleted.
retention.neverHint: Nothing is destroyed on a timer. Deleted communities stay in the list below until somebody restores one.
retention.saved_one: Deleted communities are kept for {{count}} day.
retention.saved_other: Deleted communities are kept for {{count}} days.
retention.save: Save how long communities are kept

accountRetention.title: Keeping deleted accounts
accountRetention.description: A deleted account disappears for everyone else straight away and keeps everything it holds. It is erased when this window ends, unless its holder signs back in or an operator restores it.
accountRetention.label: Keep accounts for (days)
accountRetention.hint: Counted from the moment each account was deleted, so changing this moves the date for ones already deleted.
accountRetention.neverHint: Nothing is erased on a timer. Deleted accounts stay in the users table until somebody comes back or restores one.
accountRetention.saved_one: Deleted accounts are kept for {{count}} day.
accountRetention.saved_other: Deleted accounts are kept for {{count}} days.
accountRetention.save: Save how long accounts are kept

community.engagementRankingLabel: Let communities rank results by engagement
community.engagementRankingHelpText: When off, no community on this server ranks by engagement, whatever its own setting.
community.engagementRankingEnabledToast: Communities can rank results by engagement.
community.engagementRankingDisabledToast: Engagement ranking is off for every community.
community.guestsEnabledHelpText: Communities can invite people for a set number of days. Guests take no seat and see only what they were given. While this is off, no guest gets in.
community.maxGuestDaysHelpText: No guest stays longer than this, whatever a community sets.
community.publicRegistrationHelpText: People can make an account without an invite. While community creation is off, only invited people can sign up.
community.publicRegistrationDisabledToast: Only invited people can sign up.
community.communityCreationHelpText: When off, only people who manage communities on this server can create one, and only invited people can sign up.
community.communityCreationDisabledToast: Only people who manage communities can create one.
community.creationDailyLimitLabel: Communities one account may create per day
community.creationDailyLimitHelpText: 0 means no limit. People who manage communities are not held to it.
community.creationDailyLimitSaved_one: Each account may create {{count}} community a day.
community.creationDailyLimitSaved_other: Each account may create {{count}} communities a day.
community.creationDailyLimitSavedNone: There is no daily limit on new communities.
community.exportCooldownHelpText: How long a community waits before it can export everything again. 0 means no wait.
community.exportCooldownSave: Save the time between community exports

account.passwordDescription: Change it here. You will stay signed in on this device.
account.setPasswordDescription: Your account signs in without one. Set a password here to have another way in.
account.removePasswordFromBrowser: Give your password up from a browser signed in to this site.
account.removePasswordBody: Your passkey signs you in from now on, and you will be signed out everywhere else. If your passkey is ever lost, a recovery code is what sets a new password. If you hold fewer than three codes, you'll be shown a fresh set — save them.
account.removePasswordCodes: Save these somewhere safe. If your passkey is ever lost, a recovery code is what sets a new password. Each code works once, and you won't be shown these again. Any codes you held before have stopped working.

dm.title: Direct messages
dm.description: Who can ask to message you, outside your connections.
dm.communityHint: People you share a community with.
dm.ageLocked: Messaging is available to people aged 16 and over. You have not told us whether you are.

receipts.label: Tell people when their messages reach you
receipts.help: They see when a message arrived on one of your devices and when you read it. Switch this off and they see neither — the same as somebody who has not opened the app. You still see theirs.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Connections are mutual. You can keep in touch even if you stop sharing a community.
connections.empty: You have not connected with anyone yet.
connections.addHint: Type someone's full handle, including the number.

ignored.title: Ignored accounts
ignored.description: You will not be notified when these accounts mention, reply to or react to you, and nothing they send you arrives — messages, message requests, connection requests. You will still see each other's activity in communities you share, and be able to use all tools normally.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.unanswered: You haven't answered the cookie question in this browser yet. Until you do, nothing optional is switched on.
cookies.noneAllowed: Nothing optional is switched on in this browser.
cookies.perBrowser: Your answer follows your account, so a new browser or device won't ask again. Answered before you signed in, it stays in that browser until you do.

engagementRanking.title: Search ranking
engagementRanking.label: Count my activity toward search ranking
engagementRanking.help: When on, the items you open and change help decide what your communities' search lists first. Nobody can see what you opened. Turn it off and your activity stops counting from the next hourly update.
engagementRanking.error: Couldn't save your search ranking choice. Try again.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.description: Ask for a code from an authenticator app after a password or emailed code, and whenever a community or this server asks for a second factor.
twoFactor.notSetUp: Signing in doesn't ask for a code from an app.
twoFactor.scanPrompt: Scan this with your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
twoFactor.cannotScan: Can't scan it? Enter this key instead:
twoFactor.codesPrompt: Save these somewhere safe. They are how you get in if you lose your phone.
twoFactor.codesWarning: Each code works once, and you won't be shown these again.
twoFactor.regeneratePrompt: Confirm your password. The codes you have now will stop working.
twoFactor.turnOffPrompt: Signing in will stop asking for a code from your app, and your recovery codes will be discarded. You'll be signed out on your other devices.
twoFactor.codeOrRecoveryLabel: Code from your app, or a recovery code
twoFactor.enrolError: Could not start setting that up.
twoFactor.confirmError: That code isn't right. Check your app and try again.
twoFactor.statusError: Couldn't check whether two-factor is on. Reload the page to try again.
twoFactor.copyUnavailable: Couldn't copy — write the codes down instead.
twoFactor.notOffered: This deployment does not offer the authenticator app.
twoFactor.passwordlessCodes: Your account signs in without a password. These codes are how you set one again if you lose your passkey.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in with your device's fingerprint, face or screen lock instead of your password.
passkeys.listError: Couldn't check which passkeys this account holds. Reload the page to try again.
passkeys.emptyHint: A passkey lives on your phone, your laptop or your password manager, and works only on this site.
passkeys.addPrompt: Give it a name you'll recognise later. Your browser asks for the rest.
passkeys.prompting: Follow your browser's prompt to finish.
passkeys.promptingHint: Your browser or password manager is asking you to confirm. Nothing more to do here.
passkeys.renamePrompt: This name is only for you, so you can tell your passkeys apart.
passkeys.removeConfirm: {{name}} will stop signing you in. You can add another whenever you like.
passkeys.cancelled: You cancelled, or the prompt timed out.
passkeys.alreadyRegistered: This device or password manager already holds a passkey for this site.
passkeys.siteMismatch: A passkey can't be made at this address — it doesn't match the address this site is set up under. Whoever runs the site can put that right.
passkeys.browserError: Your browser couldn't make the passkey. Try again.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser can't make a passkey. Open this page in an up-to-date browser instead.
passkeys.siteUnsupported: Passkeys need this site to have a proper domain name and https. Whoever runs it can put that right.
passkeys.limitReached: This account holds as many passkeys as it can ({{limit}}). Remove one to add another.
passkeys.addFromBrowser: A passkey is added from a browser signed in to this site. Add opens one for you.
passkeys.notOffered: This site doesn't offer passkeys. The ones you have are kept.

providerDefaults.title: What a community inherits
providerDefaults.description: Answer once for a provider and every community inherits that answer until it gives its own. Useful where this deployment is one organisation: one provider, one tenant, communities that are its teams.
providerDefaults.noAnswer: No answer — each community says for itself
providerDefaults.noProviders: Add a sign-in provider first, then say what communities inherit from it.
providerDefaults.valuesHint: Separate several with commas. A community's own connection replaces this outright, so nothing here is merged with what a community says.

platformSecurity.description: How long anybody may stay signed in, the captcha asked of anybody new, and what a notification may leave the app carrying.

notificationDelivery.title: Notifications that leave the app
notificationDelivery.description: Every community is held to these as a ceiling. A community can narrow them for itself; none can widen them.

push.label: Phone and desktop notifications
push.onHelp: Notifications reach phones through Apple and Google, and the desktop app directly.
push.offHelp: This server sends nothing to a phone or the desktop app, and stores no device registrations.

email.label: Email notifications
email.onHelp: Notifications reach mailboxes on whatever schedule each person has chosen.
email.offHelp: No notification email is sent. Sign-in codes, address confirmations, password resets and account notices still go.

redact.label: Hide notification details
redact.onHelp: A notification that leaves the app says the kind of thing that happened — “You were mentioned in a comment”. The app itself shows all of it.
redact.offHelp: A notification that leaves the app names what it is about: who acted, and on what.

communityNotifications.title: Notifications that leave the app
communityNotifications.description: What this community's notifications carry once they leave. The server answers the same three questions for everybody, and the stricter answer applies.

push.label: Phone and desktop notifications
push.onHelp: This community's notifications reach members' phones and desktop apps.
push.offHelp: Nothing about this community is sent to a phone or the desktop app. Members still get the bell, and email if it is on.
push.platformHelp: This server sends nothing to a phone or the desktop app, so there is nothing here to decide.

email.label: Email notifications
email.onHelp: This community's notifications reach members' mailboxes.
email.offHelp: No notification email is sent about this community. Sign-in codes and password resets are the account's own and still go.
email.platformHelp: This server sends no notification email, so there is nothing here to decide.

redact.label: Hide notification details
redact.onHelp: Notifications about this community say the kind of thing that happened once they leave the app. Members see all of it here.
redact.offHelp: Notifications about this community name what they are about once they leave the app.
redact.platformHelp: This server hides notification details everywhere, so this community is already covered.

communityEngagementRanking.title: Search order
communityEngagementRanking.label: Rank search results by community engagement
communityEngagementRanking.help: Search lists what more members have recently opened or worked on higher. Only a rough level is kept for each item, never who opened it or how many times, and it's never shared outside this community.
communityEngagementRanking.platformHelp: This server has turned engagement ranking off for every community.

billingInsights.title: Billing insights
billingInsights.description: How the business is doing, across every community: revenue, subscribers and cancellations.
billingInsights.fromPaddle: Revenue, recurring revenue, refunds, chargebacks and subscriber counts come straight from the payment processor, as it computed them.
billingInsights.fromBilling: Communities by plan, trials, overdue payments and cancellations come from the billing service's own records.
billingInsights.noCommunity: It opens no community and needs no access grant: nothing on the page names a community, a customer or a person.
billingInsights.openError: Billing insights could not be opened.
billingInsights.notConfigured: This deployment has no billing service to open, or no handoff signing key.
billingInsights.platformOnly: Billing insights are for platform operators and owners.

billingContracts.title: Contracts
billingContracts.description: The enterprise customers invoiced by hand, outside the payment processor.
billingContracts.invoices: Each contract's terms, the invoices issued in QuickBooks, and when they were paid.
billingContracts.keys: A dedicated deployment's registration key file, to commit to the packages repository for signing.
billingContracts.noCommunity: It opens no community and needs no access grant. A community is put on a contract from its own billing operations console.
billingContracts.openError: The contracts console could not be opened.

billingDirectory.title: Directory
billingDirectory.description: Every account that pays, in one list: the Paddle customers and the contracts.
billingDirectory.lists: Each account's communities, their plans and status, the next charge or invoice due, a dedicated deployment's key, and what reconciliation found.
billingDirectory.readOnly: Read-only. Act on an account from its community's billing consoles, under their own access grants.
billingDirectory.ownersOnly: Owners only: it names every paying customer at once.
billingDirectory.openError: The directory could not be opened.

billingControl.title: Control
billingControl.description: Where this server's plans are defined: what each plan allows, its words in each language, and the prices that sell it.
billingControl.revisions: Every change is saved as a new revision of the catalog, with who made it.
billingControl.ownersOnly: Owners only: it changes what every community is sold and allowed.
billingControl.noCommunity: It opens no community and needs no access grant.

customRoles.title: Roles
customRoles.description: A custom role gives a member part of running the community, or narrows an admin to part of it. Each person holds one at most.
customRoles.dialogDescription: Name it, choose who it is for, and tick what it holds.

rungHelp.member: Gives a member what it holds, on top of what they already do.
rungHelp.admin: Narrows an admin to what it holds.

customRoles.rungFixed: Who a role is for can't change once it is made.
customRoles.notYours: You don't hold this yourself, so you can't give it.
customRoles.empty: This community has no custom roles.
customRoles.closed: Whoever runs this server has closed custom roles for this community. The roles it has keep applying.
customRoles.deleteDescription: People holding it go back to their plain role.
customRoles.appliesWhileMember: Applies while they are a member
customRoles.appliesWhileAdmin: Applies while they are an admin

profile.label: Profile
profile.description: Change the community's name, picture, banner and description.

invites.label: Invites
invites.description: Make and delete invite links, guest invites included.

members.label: Members
members.description: Change people's roles and names, remove them, and give custom roles.

initiatives.label: Initiatives
initiatives.description: Create, archive and delete any initiative, and run ones they are not in.

community_calendars.label: Community calendars
community_calendars.description: Add and change the community's own calendars.

trash.label: Trash
trash.description: Restore or delete for good anything in the community's trash.

usage.label: Usage
usage.description: See what the community uses against its limits.

roles.label: Roles
roles.description: Add, change and delete custom roles.

customRoles.beyondYours: You can't change this role: it holds something you don't.
customRoles.widensAnAdmin: Only an admin who holds everything can delete an admin role: its holders get everything back.

customRoleRules.title: Custom roles by group
customRoleRules.description: Give a custom role to whoever signs in carrying a group. A sign-in reads these in order and the first group it carries decides; a role somebody gave by hand stays theirs.
customRoleRules.empty: No group gives a custom role yet.
customRoleRules.removeDescription: People in {{group}} keep the role it gave until they next sign in.
customRoleRules.dialogDescription: Whoever signs in through this provider carrying the group gets the role, unless an earlier rule matches first.
